layer1_to_7_text_ontology_memory_cycle.reply:
[E1] Entity record
STEM_CONCEPT:STEM-THIN-FILM-INTERFERENCE: Thin-Film Interference with Single Phase Inversion (Optics)
Description: When light in air (n_air = 1.00) reflects normally off a thin film of oil (n_film = 1.50, thickness d = 500 nm) floating on water (n_water = 1.33), reflection at the top air->oil interface (n1 < n2) undergoes a 180-degree (pi, lambda/2) phase shift, while reflection at the bottom oil->water interface (n2 > n3, 1.50 > 1.33) has NO phase shift. Constructive interference (strongest reflection) therefore satisfies 2 * n_film * d = (m + 1/2) * lambda_air.
• [MEM-CORR-PER-LAYER-PARTITION-002] (correction, epistemic=externally_verified): When a measurement shows a flat response across all settings of a parameter, suspect the structure being measured (global eviction across layers), not the effect: partitioning the same 51.7 GB cache per layer increased the hit rate from 23.3% to 48.0%.
• [MEM-HYP-CACHE-DEAD-END-001] (hypothesis, epistemic=hypothesis): Mistaken initial hypothesis that expert caching is ineffective for Kimi K3 because varying cache capacity from 512 to 4096 produced a flat 23.3% hit rate (superseded by MEM-CORR-PER-LAYER-PARTITION-002).
• [MEM-CONCEPT-FLAT-RESPONSE-DIAGNOSIS-001] (concept, epistemic=externally_verified): When varying a capacity or budget parameter across a wide range yields a completely flat metric, suspect the structure being measured (such as shared-pool cyclic eviction across stages/layers or unallocated capacity) before concluding the underlying mechanism has no effect; test partitioning the same total budget per stage/layer.
